articles.title: Pakistan steps up airport screening amid Ebola outbreak in Africa - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's health ministry has intensified airport screening measures and directed all provinces to remain on alert following the recent Ebola outbreak in Africa. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) and World Health Organisation’s (WHO) offices in Pakistan are monitoring the situation, while the ministry emphasized that the risk to Pakistan is extremely low due to limited travel links with affected countries.  The ministry also confirmed that it possesses the capacity to diagnose Ebola and has issued directives for preparedness measures.

articles.title: Failing chemical tank forces thousands to evacuate in Southern California | Environment News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of residents in Southern California have been ordered to evacuate their homes after a storage tank containing hazardous chemicals began to fail. The Orange County Fire Authority and Garden Grove Police Department are working to stabilize the situation, with firefighters attempting to reduce the tank's temperature and prevent it from leaking or exploding.  GKN Aerospace, where the tank is located, has urged residents to evacuate immediately as officials warn that a rupture could create a plume of flammable vapors.

articles.title: Senegal President Faye sacks prime minister Sonko after months or tensions
articles.rephrased_article: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye of Senegal has dismissed Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko and dissolved the government, citing months of tensions between them. The decree followed a parliamentary session where Sonko criticized Faye.  The move comes amid mounting economic pressure in the country, with its public debt exceeding 132% of GDP. Sonko, who enjoys widespread popularity among young Senegalese, has vowed to "sleep with a light heart" despite the dismissal.

articles.title: Board of Peace focus on Hamas risks return to war in Gaza, critics say | Israel-Gaza war | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza, blamed Hamas for the stalled ceasefire, accusing it of refusing to accept verified decommissioning and relinquish coercive control. However, Hamas rejected these accusations, stating that the report reflects a biased Israeli position and serves as an attempt to justify further escalation. Critics argue that Mladenov's report unfairly blames Hamas, potentially legitimizing Benjamin Netanyahu's potential return to war.  Despite Israel's continued airstrikes and expansion of its control over Gaza, the NCAG, tasked with overseeing disarmament, has been prevented from entering Gaza by Israeli authorities.

articles.title: Stephen Hawking’s father worried his son ‘does not study much’, diaries reveal | Stephen Hawking | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Hawking, a world-renowned physicist and author of "A Brief History of Time," defied medical expectations after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease at age 21.  His father, Frank Hawking, expressed concerns about his son's future in previously unknown diaries that have been made available to biographer Graham Farmelo. The diaries offer a glimpse into Hawking's formative years and the challenges he faced, including his struggle with his illness and his father's disappointment.  Farmelo's biography, "Hawking," will be published on September 24th by John Murray.

articles.title: Oil prices settle higher on slow progress in US-Iran peace talks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent and WTI crude oil futures experienced gains on Friday, driven by shifting expectations for a peace deal between Iran and the U.S.  Diplomatic sources indicated progress in talks, with Pakistan's army chief traveling to Iran, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed optimism about potential resolution. However, uncertainties remain regarding Iran's uranium stockpile and control over the Strait of Hormuz, and global oil inventories continue to deplete due to reduced oil flows through the strait.  Analysts predict a modest increase in July production by OPEC+ members, but full oil flow through the strait is not expected until the first or second quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Nagaland intensifies ASF containment measures; pork sale banned in several districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nagaland's government has intensified surveillance and containment measures following the outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF).  Several districts have imposed bans and restrictions on pig imports, transportation, and sales to prevent further spread. The Directorate of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services is actively engaged in surveillance, containment, awareness campaigns, sample collection, and bio-security measures.  The ASF outbreak has led to the temporary closure of pork shops in several parts of the state and a significant impact on local consumption patterns and livelihoods for pig farmers and traders.

articles.title: Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder past Spurs for 2-1 NBA playoff lead | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the San Antonio Spurs 123-108 in Game 3 of their Western Conference Finals series, taking a 2-1 lead.  Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder with 26 points while Jared McCain and Jaylin Williams contributed significant bench scoring. The Spurs' early 15-point lead was overcome by the Thunder, who capitalized on strong performances from Gilgeous-Alexander and a dominant second quarter. The intensity of the game escalated in the third quarter with a physical altercation between players, but the Thunder maintained their advantage throughout the fourth to secure the victory.  Game four will be played in San Antonio on Sunday.

articles.title: Rs50,000 fine in Punjab for illegal offal disposal on Eid - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz ordered a Rs50,000 fine for throwing animal waste and offal in streets during Eidul Azha. She directed authorities to remain vigilant at cattle markets and enforce bans on illegal livestock trading, hide collection by banned organizations, loudspeakers use at hide-collection camps, and display of weapons and aerial firing.  Ms Nawaz also emphasized the importance of maintaining ecological balance and ensuring the survival of life on Earth through effective measures for protecting endangered species and conserving the ecosystem.

articles.title: Multimedia arts project wins Sycamore Gap tree commission after public vote | Art and design | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Helix Arts and George King Architects won a public vote to create a "living archive" from preserved wood of the felled Sycamore Gap tree. The project, “The People’s Tree,” will use participatory storytelling, sound, and sculpture to celebrate the beloved sycamore and capture memories of its loss.  It will involve communities across the UK, including those who haven't had access to nature, through interactive elements like a digital archive and co-created artworks. The project is expected to be completed by autumn 2027 and will include the planting of 49 "trees of hope" saplings across the UK.

articles.title: Dollar near six-week high amid Iran war jitters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's foreign minister met with Pakistan's interior minister to discuss proposals for ending the U.S.-Israeli conflict, according to Iranian media reports.  Traders are concerned about ongoing energy disruptions and their impact on consumer prices, potentially forcing a tighter monetary policy response from the Federal Reserve. The dollar index rose slightly while the yen weakened against the greenback as rising oil prices and persistent inflation pressures continue to affect global markets.

articles.title: Sulur minor girl abduction and murder: Law and order a serious concern in T.N., says Udhayanidhi Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhayanidhi Stalin, leader of the Opposition, expressed concern over 30 major crimes within 12 days of the new government assuming office. These incidents include sexual violence, ganja smuggling, and the abduction and murder of a minor girl in Coimbatore. Stalin called for swift justice for the victim's family and urged the Chief Minister to prioritize law and order to prevent future incidents.

articles.title: Iran war day 85: Tehran says major gaps remain in US talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran to intensify diplomatic efforts for a US-Iran peace deal. Iranian officials acknowledged significant gaps remain between the two sides despite ongoing talks and emphasized that ending the war is essential for any future agreement.  While Qatar has been praised for supporting Pakistani-led mediation efforts, tensions remain over Iran’s enriched uranium program and control of the Strait of Hormuz. The US continues to engage in diplomatic efforts with Iran, but major differences persist. Meanwhile, escalating violence between Israel and Lebanon has resulted in casualties and strained the Lebanese economy.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX carries out mostly successful Starship test flight - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully conducted a test flight of its Starship spacecraft, which splashed down into the Indian Ocean after a mostly successful journey. The third-generation Starship carried out maneuvers including flipping upright and reigniting its engines despite one malfunctioning during an initial burn. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, praised his team's efforts on X, calling it "epic".  The company is preparing for a potentially record initial public offering in June.

articles.title: Anthony Albanese visibly emotional after defending Labor’s capital gains tax and negative gearing changes | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Albanese, the prime minister, defended his government's proposed changes to negative gearing, capital gains tax (CGT), and family trusts. He argued that these reforms are necessary to rebalance the housing market in favor of first-time home buyers and ensure a fairer system for working Australians.  Albanese emphasized that Labor is committed to supporting aspiration for all, including young people who struggle to enter the housing market. While some Labor MPs expressed concerns about the potential negative impact on property investors, Chris Bowen, the energy minister, stated that these changes are crucial for intergenerational equity and acknowledged that they may be controversial but ultimately beneficial.  The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, criticized the budget as an attack on young Australians and a threat to their aspirations.

articles.title: Planning SIPs for a car or house in 10 years? Experts recommend diversified equity funds for long-term goals - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Pankaj Mathpal, MD of Optima Money Managers, advised viewers seeking to invest through SIPs with a 10-year horizon to consider diversified equity funds like ICICI Prudential Midcap Fund, Motilal Oswal Large and Midcap Fund, Bajaj Finserv Flexicap Fund, and HDFC Midcap Fund. He cautioned against investing in gold ETFs due to the government's efforts to reduce gold imports and recommended a focus on diversified mutual funds and multi-asset allocation funds for risk management. Mathpal also warned against excessive exposure to thematic or sectoral funds without understanding market cycles and emphasized that investors with limited knowledge should stick to these strategies.

articles.title: 'Poor thing': Iran mocks Donald Trump as viral buffalo resembling him loses appetite - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran shared a viral video of a Bangladeshi albino buffalo resembling Donald Trump, claiming the animal lost its appetite due to comparisons to the US president. The buffalo, named "Donald Trump," has become a popular attraction in Bangladesh ahead of Eid al-Adha.  The US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, triggering weeks of escalating tensions between the two countries. Trump met with senior officials to discuss potential military action against Iran if negotiations fail. Diplomatic efforts are underway through Pakistan Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir's visit to Tehran and a Qatari delegation's arrival in Iran.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh woman killed by boyfriend after she refuses to accompany him - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ali Mohammad, 25, has been arrested for allegedly strangling his 21-year-old girlfriend, Reshma, inside her home in Uttar Pradesh's Shamli district. The incident occurred on Friday evening, with family members present.  Police say Ali Mohammad attacked Reshma after she refused to accompany him somewhere and both he and his associate, Aliyas, were apprehended at the scene. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, and police are continuing their investigation.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Which star players will miss the tournament? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Several high-profile players will miss the 2026 World Cup in North America due to injuries or failed qualifying. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, a standout winger for Georgia, won't be at the tournament after his country failed to qualify.  Robert Lewandowski, a veteran striker for Poland, hinted at international retirement following their failure to qualify, while Gianluigi Donnarumma and Sandro Tonali, key players for Italy, will also miss out due to the Azzurri's disappointing qualifying campaign. Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman of Nigeria are another notable absence after a shock penalty shootout defeat in the African playoffs.  Hugo Ekitike suffered an Achilles tendon injury, while Estevao and Rodrygo, both from Brazil, were sidelined by hamstring and knee injuries respectively.

articles.title: Rubio starts first visit to India on heels of US-China summit - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio began a four-day visit to India, focusing on strengthening ties with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  Rubio's first stop was in Kolkata, where he visited the headquarters of Mother Teresa's charity and prayed over her tomb. He then traveled to New Delhi, where he is scheduled to meet with Modi later on Saturday. During his visit, Rubio will also participate in a meeting of foreign ministers from the Quad, a group of democracies seeking to counter China's influence in the Indian Ocean.  The trip comes as President Donald Trump has shifted US priorities and relations with both India and China have become more complex.

articles.title: One dead in NYC's Staten Island after shipyard explosion
articles.rephrased_article: A barge explosion at a Staten Island shipyard on Friday injured over 30 people, including firefighters and first responders.  One civilian died in the incident, which began with reports of workers trapped and a fire. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani declared it a complex emergency situation, prompting additional responders to the scene. The cause of the fire and explosion is under investigation.

articles.title: Albanese joins coalition of nations calling for an end to Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Albanese and leaders of the UK, Italy, France, Germany, Canada, Norway, the Netherlands, and New Zealand issued a joint statement condemning Israeli government policies in the West Bank as they undermine stability and prospects for peace. The statement called out the E1 settlement project, which would connect occupied territories in East Jerusalem with another Israeli settlement, as a breach of international law.  The leaders urged Israel to end its expansion of settlements and administrative powers, ensure accountability for settler violence, investigate allegations against Israeli forces, respect the Hashemite custodianship over Jerusalem's Holy Sites, and lift financial restrictions on the Palestinian Authority.

articles.title: Paytm block deal: SocGen, Ghisallo, Viridian among biggest buyers in Rs 964 crore stake sale - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Societe Generale, Ghisallo Master Fund LP, and Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund were among the largest buyers in a recent transaction of Paytm shares, totaling approximately Rs 964 crore.  Domestic institutional investors such as Nippon India Mutual Fund and Sundaram Mutual Fund also participated in the deal. The stock closed down on Friday by 3.74%, settling at Rs 1,112.40 after a year of strong gains driven by improved operational metrics and investor confidence.  Global investment bank Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius is reported to have been appointed as the placement agent for the transaction.

articles.title: China coal mine blast: 90 killed after gas explosion in Shanxi; rescue operations for trapped under way - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A gas explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi province, China, killed at least 90 people and trapped hundreds of workers underground. Chinese President Xi Jinping directed rescuers to prioritize finding missing miners and ensuring a thorough investigation into the cause of the blast.  Premier Li Qiang echoed these sentiments, demanding swift action and accountability for those responsible. The explosion occurred on Friday evening and rescue efforts are still underway.

articles.title: Ponraj gets anticipatory bail over remarks on TVK women supporters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a political commentator, has been granted anticipatory bail by the Madras High Court in two criminal cases related to derogatory remarks against women supporters of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The court imposed conditions requiring him to appear before police twice a week and once a week, as well as refrain from threatening witnesses or tampering with evidence.  The judge acknowledged the intent behind Ponraj's statements but granted bail due to his strong ties to society and low risk of absconding.

articles.title: Gas explosion at Chinese coal mine kills at least 90 | Mining News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A gas explosion at a coal mine in Qinyuan county, Shanxi province, has killed at least 90 people. The blast occurred at the Liushenyu mine, where 247 workers were on duty when the explosion ripped through the facility.  President Xi Jinping called for intensified efforts to prevent major accidents following the incident. Rescue operations are ongoing as emergency crews search for survivors. Xinhua, the state-run broadcaster, reported that the person responsible for overseeing the mine has been arrested while authorities investigate the cause of the explosion.

articles.title: China coal mine blast kills at least 90, more missing - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A gas explosion at a coal mine in Shanxi province, China, has killed at least 82 people and left nine others unaccounted for. President Xi Jinping ordered "all-out efforts" to treat the injured and called for thorough investigations into the incident. The blast occurred on Friday evening at the Liushenyu coal mine, where 247 workers were underground.  The death toll is expected to rise as rescue efforts continue.

articles.title: At least 82 dead in Chinese coal mine explosion, state media reports
articles.rephrased_article: At least 90 people have been killed in a coal mine explosion at the Liushenyu Coal Mine in Shanxi Province, China. The blast occurred on Friday evening and was caused by a gas explosion, according to state media reports. Chinese President Xi Jinping called for full efforts to rescue survivors and investigate the cause of the accident.  The Ministry of Emergency Management has sent personnel from six rescue teams to assist with the operation.

articles.title: China mine explosion: death toll leaps to 90 after gas blast | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A gas explosion at a coalmine in Shanxi province, China has resulted in at least 90 fatalities.  The incident occurred on Friday evening at the Liushenyu mine, trapping 247 workers underground. President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang have called for swift rescue efforts and investigations into the cause of the accident. The local emergency management authority is leading the search and rescue operations while authorities detain executives from the mine's operator.

articles.title: Dar to advance diplomatic push at UNSC moot - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Ishaq Dar, will attend a UN Security Council meeting convened by China on May 26th to discuss maintaining international peace and security.  The meeting, chaired by Wang Yi, is expected to feature participation from Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, as well as foreign ministers from several countries including Pakistan, Iran, Cambodia, Costa Rica, Bahrain, Turkmenistan, the Czech Republic, Colombia, and Azerbaijan. The session will also include representatives from all five permanent Security Council members: the United States, China, Russia, France, and the United Kingdom.

articles.title: Olympic rower floats like astronaut to test future space gym
articles.rephrased_article: Matthew Wells, a former Olympic athlete, is participating in parabolic flight tests to evaluate the effectiveness of HIFIm, a new exercise device designed for astronauts. The device, developed by a consortium including Esa, Nasa, and the UK Space Agency, aims to reduce the time astronauts spend exercising while maintaining muscle mass and bone density during space missions.  Dr Meganne Christian, a reserve astronaut for Esa and Senior Exploration Manager at the UK Space Agency, believes this technology could significantly impact astronaut health and mission success.

articles.title: For every job at Mazagon Dock, 6.4 jobs are created across economy: Captain Jagmohan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Captain Jagmohan (Retd.), Chairman and Managing Director of Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), stated that one direct job at MDL generates six and a half jobs across India. He cited the Project 17A frigate as an example, where 4,500 MDL workers support nearly 28,000 positions in ancillary industries. The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision (MAKV) aims to place India among the top five shipbuilding countries by 2047 with a target of 4.5 million gross tonnage and an expected investment of ₹4.5 lakh crore.

articles.title: Unlike Centre, Sindh announces four Eid holidays - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah issued a notification extending the Eidul Azha holiday in the province to four days, from May 26th to May 29th, 2026. The holiday applies to all government offices, autonomous bodies, semi-autonomous bodies, corporations, and local councils, except for essential services and departments/offices preparing the budget for the fiscal year 2026-27.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak: 'Speed, money and compassion' - lessons from a survivor and other experts
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of Congo is grappling with a new Ebola outbreak, prompting comparisons to the devastating 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.  Patrick Faley, an Ebola survivor from Liberia, recalls the horrors of that crisis and warns against complacency. He emphasizes the importance of community trust, safe burials, and clear communication in controlling outbreaks. Dr. Patrick Otim, the WHO's area manager for Africa, stresses the need for swift action, emphasizing early detection and isolation as crucial to containing transmission.  Professor Thomas Geisbert, a leading Ebola expert, highlights the lack of an effective vaccine for Bundibugyo, a rare strain of the virus, while urging investment in research and development. The WHO is prioritizing the use of experimental anti-viral drug Obladesivir, but experts warn that containment efforts must be swift to prevent further spread.

articles.title: US jury finds Boeing not guilty in 737 MAX grounding lawsuit - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A US jury ruled in favor of Boeing, finding the aerospace giant not liable for lost revenue claims from Polish airline LOT. LOT had accused Boeing of fraud and sought $250 million in compensation for alleged false representations concerning its 737 MAX jets, which were grounded for 20 months following two deadly crashes.  The jury's decision comes after a series of lawsuits related to the MAX crashes, including settlements with victim families and a criminal charge dismissal against Boeing as part of an agreement with US prosecutors.

articles.title: Five killed in cruiser-lorry collision near Wadi in Kalaburagi district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A head-on collision between a cruiser vehicle and an Ashok Leyland lorry on National Highway 150 near Neeladahalla, India, resulted in the deaths of five people from Ingalagi village. The accident occurred early Saturday morning when the cruiser, driven by Mashaq Saab, collided with the lorry transporting goods from Gujarat to Chennai.

articles.title: Green card seekers must leave US first - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced a new policy requiring most foreigners seeking permanent residency to apply for immigrant visas from abroad. The change, part of President Trump's immigration strategy, restricts the "adjustment of status" process within the US.  Applicants currently in the US on temporary visas will be expected to pursue green cards through consular processing overseen by the US Department of State. The policy is expected to affect families and applicants with US-born children.

articles.title: More than 40,000 evacuated in Orange County due to chemical tank leak
articles.rephrased_article: Over 40,000 people in southern California have been evacuated from their homes due to a chemical leak at an aerospace manufacturing facility. The Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) issued evacuation orders after reports of a tank temperature increase and expanded the zone as authorities investigate the cause of the leak.  OCFA Chief Craig Covey stated that there are three tanks at the facility, with one having a compromised cooling system, and two potential outcomes: the tank failing and spilling chemicals or going into a thermal runaway explosion.

articles.title: Marco Rubio in India LIVE: Rubio visits Saint Teresa's Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State, began a four-day diplomatic tour to India on Saturday (May 23, 2026), visiting Kolkata as the first stop. The trip is significant for its focus on energy talks with India and meetings with Ministers from the Quad nations.  Rubio's visit comes amid heightened tensions in the Persian Gulf region, which has impacted India's energy security.

articles.title: ‘Big guns’ descend on Tehran as talks enter decisive phase - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of Defence Forces of Pakistan, arrived in Tehran to participate in mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.  The visit came as negotiations progressed towards a ceasefire extension, sanctions relief, and maritime security guarantees. While some progress was reported, key issues like Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile remain unresolved. The US has indicated it would consider a "Plan B" involving Nato countries if Iran refuses to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, emphasized Washington's commitment to preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons and expressed hope for an agreement but acknowledged that more work is needed.  Qatar joined mediation efforts alongside the United States, while Saudi Arabia also engaged with Iranian officials. Regional diplomats highlighted a shift towards stabilization efforts rather than comprehensive settlement negotiations.

articles.title: California: 40,000 people ordered to evacuate over chemical leak fears | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: GKN Aerospace, a British corporation, faced a chemical leak at its facility in Garden Grove, California, prompting the evacuation of 40,000 residents. The storage tank holding methyl methacrylate began off-gassing and threatened to fail, with authorities initially responding with a hazmat team but later issuing new evacuation orders due to further damage. Orange county fire authority division chief Craig Covey warned that the situation could result in either a spill or a thermal runaway explosion, urging residents to heed evacuation orders.

articles.title: UFO sighting reports released by US government - 'Orbs swarming in all directions'
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon released scores of UFO files on Friday, containing descriptions and videos of unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) dating back to 1948. The documents include witness accounts, audio recordings, and video footage, some showing UAP being shot down by military aircraft.  These releases follow an order from President Donald Trump earlier this year. While the Pentagon has not drawn any definitive conclusions about extraterrestrial life or alien technology, they have stated that people can decide for themselves what these phenomena are.

articles.title: Retail players can skip Central Bank of India OFS, say analysts, cite margin and earnings concerns - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre is selling up to an 8% stake in the State Bank of India (SBI) through an initial public offering (OFS).  Investors are advised to avoid participating due to concerns about profitability and a potential supply overhang. The retail portion of the OFS opens on Monday, with the floor price set at ₹31 per share, a discount of 8.6% from Thursday's closing price. Analysts suggest caution as further stake sales may be necessary to meet public shareholding requirements.

articles.title: YouTuber Danny Go’s son Isaac Coleman’s cause of death: Inside the 14-year-old’s battle with rare illness | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Danny Go, a popular YouTube creator known for his children's content, shared the tragic news of his son Isaac Coleman's death at age 14 on May 21, 2026. Isaac had Fanconi anemia, a rare inherited disorder that significantly increased his risk of developing serious illnesses.  Following the announcement, thousands of supporters expressed their condolences and prayers for the grieving family.

articles.title: India successfully test-fires Agni-1 ballistic missile from Odisha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India successfully test-launched the short-range ballistic missile Agni-1 from the Integrated Test Range in Balasore, Odisha. The launch, conducted under the aegis of Strategic Forces Command, validated all operational and technical parameters of the missile system. This successful trial marks another milestone in maintaining India's armed forces' operational preparedness and strategic deterrence capability.

articles.title: Iran war live: Tehran says diplomacy continues but no deal yet with US | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s powerful army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran on Friday to mediate a peace agreement between Iran and the United States.  However, Iranian officials have tempered hopes for a quick resolution, citing "deep and significant" differences in mediated talks with Washington.

articles.title: PM grants four-year extension to Intelligence Bureau chief - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has approved a four-year contract extension for Fuad Asadullah Khan, the director general of the Intelligence Bureau (IB). The extension, effective July 14, 2026, consolidates Mr. Khan's position as head of the IB during a period marked by complex internal security challenges and political transitions.  Copies of the notification have been dispatched to various government entities.

articles.title: Trump Mobile investigating potential exposure of would-be customers’ personal information | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Trump Mobile, a phone company launched by Donald Trump’s family business, is investigating a potential security flaw on its website that may have exposed personal details of 27,000 people who preordered gold-colored smartphones. The company stated that it has not identified evidence of direct system compromise but is taking additional safeguards and monitoring measures. An Australian programmer discovered the vulnerability and reported it to Trump Mobile.  The incident occurred as Trump Mobile began distributing its bespoke T1 smartphones after a delay and shift in manufacturing location from the US to other locations.

articles.title: Marco Rubio visits India to sell energy as Iran oil shock persists
articles.rephrased_article: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Saturday for a four-day visit amid geopolitical tensions and an energy crisis triggered by the Iran war.  Rubio aims to sell India more energy, acknowledging the challenges facing the country's energy security. He will meet with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and discuss ways to increase US energy exports to India, which imports over 80% of its energy needs. The visit comes amid ongoing trade negotiations between India and the US, as well as tensions surrounding Pakistan and Iran.

articles.title: D-Street ends week in the green with war and peace on its mind - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The NSE Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex both closed higher on Friday, rising 0.3% each to close at 23,719.30 and 75,415.35 respectively.  Analysts predict a potential breakout for the Nifty, which could reach 25,800 levels in the coming month. While foreign portfolio investors sold shares worth ₹4,440.5 crore on Friday, domestic institutional investors bought shares worth ₹6,003.5 crore. The India VIX volatility index dropped 4.7% this week, indicating a positive short-term outlook for the market.

articles.title: Watch: SpaceX Starship bursts into flames during fiery Indian Ocean splashdown after test flight - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully completed its 12th test flight of the Starship rocket system, with the spacecraft making a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean after encountering several technical glitches. Despite issues during the mission, including an engine malfunction and a booster falling uncontrollably into the Gulf of Mexico, SpaceX celebrated the successful completion of the flight.  The company's chief, Elon Musk, expressed optimism about the future of Starship, which is central to NASA's Artemis program and faces competition from Blue Origin.

articles.title: Delhi HC seeks response from AAP’s Gopal Rai, journalist in contempt plea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gopal Rai, an AAP leader, and journalist Saurav Das were issued notices by the Delhi High Court in response to a petition seeking contempt proceedings against them for allegedly orchestrating a social media campaign against Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma. The petition also named former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal and ex-AAP MLA Saurabh Bhardwaj as parties, alleging that they exerted extra-judicial pressure on the judge through their social media posts.  The court has listed the case for further hearing on August 4th after observing that a contempt case is already underway against Kejriwal and others.

articles.title: Some fear US-Philippines war games are drawing conflict closer to home | Military News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Concerns are growing that US-Philippines military cooperation is increasing the risk of conflict. Critics argue that close alignment with Washington makes Manila a potential target in future conflicts, citing the recent Balikatan exercises as evidence. The annual joint drills, which involve thousands of soldiers from multiple countries, have been criticized for disrupting local communities and raising tensions with China.  The Philippines has received significant military aid from the US over the years, including weapons systems like Tomahawk missiles, prompting concerns about potential escalation in regional conflicts.

articles.title: Meet demands or face budget boycott, Achakzai tells govt - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mehmood Khan Achakzai, leader of the opposition in the National Assembly, warned Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif that the upcoming budget session would be a complete boycott if the government does not meet their demands for Imran Khan's medical treatment and unrestricted visitation rights.  He also criticized the lackluster attendance from the treasury benches as evidence of the government's disregard for parliament. Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, chairman of the PTI, accused the government of suppressing dissent and police excesses against those attempting to visit Imran Khan in prison.

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed 10, including six paramedics, health ministry says | Lebanon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel carried out airstrikes in Lebanon, killing 10 people including six paramedics and a child, according to the Lebanese health ministry. The strikes occurred over the past 24 hours, placing further strain on a US-brokered ceasefire.  The Israeli military claimed these strikes targeted Hezbollah infrastructure and militants. The Lebanese health ministry condemned the attacks as violations of international law and reported damage to hospitals in southern Lebanon.  These incidents have resulted in significant civilian casualties and raised concerns about the safety of healthcare workers and civilians.

articles.title: Race for French presidency sees ex-PM Philippe as early favourite to beat populists
articles.rephrased_article: Edouard Philippe, the former prime minister of Emmanuel Macron, is emerging as the frontrunner in the French presidential race.  He is seen as the only candidate capable of defeating a hard-right candidate, such as Marine Le Pen, or her deputy Jordan Bardella.  Philippe's campaign strategy focuses on appealing to center-right voters and positioning himself as a barrier against far-right populism. However, challenges remain, including potential rivalries within the center-right, the ongoing corruption probe into Philippe, and the unpredictable nature of the political landscape. The outcome of the race will likely hinge on the performance of Marine Le Pen and her party, the National Rally (RN), as well as the strength of the hard-left candidate, Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

articles.title: Patient capital trusts India as hot money exits; FDI inflow rises 17% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gross foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows increased to $94.5 billion in 2025-26 from $80.6 billion the previous year, while net FDI inflows surged to $7.7 billion from $1 billion.  The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) attributed this growth to greenfield investments in finance and technology sectors, despite a moderation in gross inflows. External commercial borrowings also decreased to $43 billion in 2025-26. The RBI noted continued pressure from foreign portfolio investor (FPI) outflows.

articles.title: 'Revenge matter of time': IRGC-trained Iraqi arrested over assassination plot against Donald Trump's daughter Ivanka - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ivanka Trump, daughter of former US President Donald Trump, was allegedly targeted for assassination by Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, a 32-year-old Iraqi national trained by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).  Al-Saadi had allegedly pledged to kill Ivanka Trump and was found with a blueprint of her Florida residence, seeking revenge for the US drone strike that killed top Iranian military commander Qasem Soleimani in 2020. Al-Saadi was arrested in Turkey and extradited to the United States where he faces charges related to 18 attacks across Europe and the US.  He is believed to have links with both Kata’ib Hezbollah and the IRGC.

articles.title: Centre tells Supreme Court it will bring back persons allegedly ‘pushed’ to Bangladesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre informed the Supreme Court of India that it will repatriate individuals deported to Bangladesh and verify their citizenship claims upon return. The government's decision comes in response to a September 2025 order from the Calcutta High Court that overturned the deportation of Sunali Khatun and others, deeming it illegal.  The court has scheduled a hearing for July.

articles.title: Why are anti-migrant attacks increasing in South Africa? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Human Rights Watch has warned of a new wave of xenophobic attacks in South Africa, fueled by anti-immigration groups like March and March and Operation Dudula. These groups are targeting foreign nationals, including Zimbabweans, with intimidation, harassment, and violence.  The situation is exacerbated by poverty, inequality, and unemployment, which have led to increased frustration and support for these vigilante groups. While the South African government maintains its commitment to protecting migrants' rights, critics argue that stricter enforcement of immigration laws is needed to address the underlying issues contributing to the attacks. The United Nations and the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights have also expressed concern over the escalating violence against migrants.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz departs on 4-day visit to China - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif departed on a four-day visit to China from May 23 to 26, accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, IT Minister Shaza Fatima, and PM’s adviser Tariq Fatemi. The visit marks the 75th anniversary of Pakistan-China diplomatic relations and will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in political, economic, and strategic domains.  The premier will meet with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang, discussing topics such as CPEC development, trade, investment, industrial cooperation, agricultural modernization, information technology, science and technology, and people-to-people exchanges.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX launches Starship V3 rocket after delays
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully launched its massive Starship V3 rocket on a test flight, marking the largest and most powerful rocket in history. The uncrewed rocket deployed 20 dummy satellites before splashing down in the Indian Ocean after an hour-long journey. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, praised the team's achievement while NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman expressed excitement for future missions to the moon and Mars.  The successful test flight, despite engine failures, is expected to boost confidence for investors and NASA as it prepares for future space endeavors.

articles.title: Centre promised more legislative powers for Ladakh, says delegation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) proposed a new mechanism to grant Ladakh greater legislative, financial, and administrative powers within the existing Union Territory framework.  Civil society members who attended a sub-committee meeting with MHA officials on Friday (May 22, 2026) reported that the talks were positive and that the MHA would soon send a draft outlining the proposed changes.

articles.title: Jana Nayagan leak case: Madras High Court denies bail to six accused - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court denied bail to six individuals who shared and watched the leaked film "Jana Nayagan" before its official release.  Justice R. Sakthivel dismissed all bail petitions after the prosecution argued that the illegal viewing of the movie by millions constituted a serious offense.

articles.title: Seven MLAs from Chennai find place in Tamil Nadu cabinet: highest in recent years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and seven other ministers from Chennai constituencies were sworn in on Thursday, marking a significant representation for the city in the new cabinet.  This is one of the highest contributions to the current cabinet from Chennai, with many top leaders from the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) contesting from the city and becoming ministers.

articles.title: TANUVAS invites applications for UG courses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Tanuvas) has opened its application portal for undergraduate courses, including Bachelor's in Veterinary Sciences and Animal Husbandry, and various B. Tech programs. Applications are open from 10 a.m. on May 25 to 5 p.m. on June 17 through the university's website: https://adm.tanuvas.ac.in.  Candidates can find details regarding seat reservations for NRIs, NRI-sponsored candidates, and foreign nationals on the portal.

articles.title: Innovation begins with understanding the fundamentals: Prakash Balasubramanian - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prakash Balasubramanian, senior director at Infineon Technologies, emphasized the importance of foundational knowledge for technological breakthroughs during the inauguration of "Nirmaan Utsav" in Kalaburagi city. He highlighted the evolution of technologies over decades and urged students to think innovatively. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Shaloo encouraged students to combine academic learning with practical experience and stay updated on emerging fields like drones, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity. HKE Society president and MLC Shashil Namoshi noted that PDA Engineering College is nurturing future-ready students through events like "Nirmaan Utsav."

articles.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed chair as Trump faces backlash over economy | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Warsh, hand-picked by Donald Trump, was sworn in as chair of the US Federal Reserve, tasked with navigating an uncertain economic outlook.  Warsh faces pressure to cut interest rates despite rising inflation and criticism over his perceived lack of independence from the president.  The new Fed chair pledged a "reform-oriented" approach while acknowledging challenges facing the economy. Public opinion polls show growing dissatisfaction with Trump's economic record, particularly regarding immigration enforcement and affordability issues. The US Federal Reserve faces mounting pressure to address these concerns as Americans grapple with rising fuel prices and inflation.

articles.title: KARD, Khandre condemn assault on BRIMS resident doctor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Association of Resident Doctors (KARD) and Bidar district in-charge Minister Eshwar B. Khandre condemned the alleged assault of a resident doctor at Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences (BRIMS), urging the state government to improve security for doctors working in public hospitals.  A letter sent to the Director of Medical Education on Friday stated that Tukaram, a 28-year-old orthopaedic resident doctor, was allegedly assaulted while attending to an injured patient in the casualty ward around 1 a.m. on Friday.

articles.title: US green card applicants will now have to return to home countries to apply, DHS says | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS announced a new policy requiring foreigners seeking green cards to apply for them outside the United States. The move, criticized by aid groups and immigration attorneys, will force many applicants to leave the country while their cases are processed, potentially impacting families and creating further strain on an already burdened system.  The agency cited the need to ensure the integrity of the immigration system and prevent loopholes, but the policy change is expected to have significant consequences for those seeking permanent residency in the US.

articles.title: Bengali actors face heat after power shift to BJP; FIR filed over 2021 social media posts linked to post-poll violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Parambrata Chatterjee, a Bengali actor, announced he had to align with the Trinamool Congress after the recent West Bengal Assembly election results.  He stated this decision was made for his one-year-old son, prompting strong reactions from social media users and fellow actors. Keya Ghosh, a BJP leader, responded by criticizing Chatterjee's compromise and highlighting the unwavering support of many BJP supporters in the state.

articles.title: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the former Democrat and former Hawaii representative, resigned as director of national intelligence on Friday.  Her tenure was marked by tension with President Donald Trump, who often excluded her from key conversations and publicly questioned her intelligence assessments. Despite efforts to streamline the agency, Gabbard's relationship with the president deteriorated over time, culminating in a public disagreement about Iran and a perceived partisan approach to her role. Following Gabbard's resignation, Aaron Lukas will serve as acting director until June 30th.

articles.title: Elected government has no role in Jammu demolitions, says Farooq Abdullah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference (NC), stated that the elected government has no involvement in the ongoing demolitions in Jammu.  He accused the opposition parties of pursuing anti-Gujjar policies and claimed that Gujjars and Bakerwals have historically protected the region's borders. Gulam Ali Khatana, a BJP Rajya Sabha member, countered by accusing the NC and Congress of neglecting the development of Gujjar and Pahari communities for decades. He praised the Modi government's efforts to empower these communities.

articles.title: SpaceX launches its biggest rocket yet in test flight from Texas | SpaceX | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX launched its largest Starship rocket, a redesigned version dubbed V3, on a test flight from Starbase in Texas. The launch carried 20 mock Starlink satellites and marked the company's 12th attempt to fly the vehicle. NASA, which is funding the project, hopes to use the Starship to land astronauts on the moon as part of its Artemis program.  SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has announced plans for an initial public offering of the company.

articles.title: Rajasthan Cabinet approves new industrial development policy with focus on talent economy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajasthan Cabinet approved a new industrial development policy focused on talent economy and private sector participation to create a world-class industrial infrastructure.  Industries and Commerce Minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore stated the policy would provide incentives for micro, small, and medium enterprises, one district one product, and the export sector. The policy aims to boost the state's economy to $350 billion by 2028-29.  The Cabinet also approved decisions on energy production, water conservation, and pensioners' welfare.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as Trump’s top US intelligence official | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, former Democratic congresswoman and presidential candidate, resigned as Donald Trump's director of national intelligence citing her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer.  She cited her decision to leave the administration in part due to her opposition to US military interventionism, which she has held since serving in the Hawaii National Guard during the Iraq War. The president confirmed Gabbard's resignation and appointed Aaron Lukas as acting director.

articles.title: Uk Airlines Offers: UK airlines EasyJet and Jet2 assure holidaymakers: No extra charges for summer flights despite rising fuel costs | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: easyJet and Jet2 have assured customers that their summer travel plans remain unaffected despite rising jet fuel prices linked to Middle Eastern tensions.  Both airlines stated they had no fuel shortages and would not introduce extra charges for flights or package holidays. However, Kenton Jarvis, chief executive of easyJet, warned that higher oil prices could eventually affect fares later in the summer. Willie Walsh, director general of the International Air Transport Association, cautioned that airlines may have to pass on rising fuel costs to passengers.

articles.title: Protester with ‘Trump is a war criminal’ banner removed from Trump rally in New York state – US politics live | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump held a rally in Rockland county, New York, where he was interrupted twice by protesters. The president then spoke about how his supporters had previously defended him from protestors and claimed that the recent disruptions were "dangerous." Trump also addressed the case of Kilmar Ábrego García, who was deported to El Salvador despite a US court order barring it. He blamed the previous administration for sending Ábrego to the prison, claiming an "administrative error".  The president then spoke about his son's upcoming wedding and claimed that he had been forced to return to Washington due to government matters. Trump boasted about passing a dementia test and recounted a story about a friend who complained about the cost of GLP-1 shots. He also announced Aaron Lukas as acting director of national intelligence after Tulsi Gabbard resigned.

articles.title: Debt and distress: youth caught in cricket betting trap - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cricket, once a beloved sport in India, has seen a surge in gambling and betting activities.  The rise of online platforms, including mobile apps and websites, has made it easier for individuals to engage in this activity, targeting vulnerable groups such as unemployed youth, students, and daily wage earners. Police are concerned about the expansion of this illegal industry into an international network.

articles.title: Israel’s October 7 tribunal: Show trial of Palestinians or justice? | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel approved a special military tribunal to try Palestinians accused of participating in the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack.  The tribunal will have the power to impose the death penalty and has drawn criticism from international organizations including the United Nations, which called for its repeal. Human rights groups like Amnesty International and B'tselem condemn the legislation as a way of seeking revenge on imprisoned Palestinians, while some Israeli parliamentarians believe it will bring justice. The tribunal is expected to hold televised trials of an estimated 300 detainees, many of whom are civilians, with concerns raised about potential unfair trials due to coercive practices in security-related cases.  The move has been met with mixed reactions, with some Israelis supporting the tribunal while others call for a state commission of inquiry into the government's role in preventing the attack.

articles.title: Drugged, raped and filmed: German woman alleges years of horrific abuse by ex-partner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A German woman, 59-year-old Claudia Wuttke, has accused her former partner of drugging and raping her over a period of 16 years, with the alleged crimes captured on video.  Police discovered the videos in June 2025 after finding them on a laptop. The German authorities dropped investigations into 65 of the 67 alleged cases due to statute of limitations laws, leaving only two remaining cases for prosecution. Wuttke expressed her disappointment at the lack of justice and called it "unacceptable" that most of the abuse would go unpunished.

articles.title: Police drop case against artist who depicted high-profile Australians in uniforms with Nazi symbols | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Agzarian, an artist, was charged with displaying Nazi symbols by a public act without lawful excuse after depicting prominent Australians in military uniforms emblazoned with Nazi symbols.  The charges were dropped before the Downing Centre local court on Friday, almost a year after they were filed. Judge Karen Stafford found that the police had reasonable cause to lay the charges but criticized them for taking seven months to withdraw them. Agzarian's lawyer argued that the artwork was political satire and that his client did not know the symbols were Nazi symbols.

articles.title: Vadodara to host Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference in June - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vibrant Gujarat Regional Conference (VGRC) will be held in Vadodara in the last week of June 2026, focusing on Central Gujarat's industrial strength and investment opportunities. The conference aims to highlight the region's contributions to manufacturing, including its dominance in sectors like transport equipment, auto components, pharmaceuticals, and beverages.  The event will attract stakeholders from industry, government, and academia, with a focus on tourism and culture. Gujarat is expected to showcase its strengths in these areas, including heritage sites like Sabarmati Ashram and the Statue of Unity.

articles.title: Burnham says politics ‘needs new script’ and vows to change Labour if elected as Makerfield MP – as it happened | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham launched his campaign as the Labour candidate in the Makerfield byelection. He stated that a vote for him is a vote to change Labour and highlighted successes of Greater Manchester and Liverpool since he left Westminster in 2017. The Green party's candidate, Chris Kennedy, withdrew from the ballot just nine hours after being announced.  John Healey, the defence secretary, urged Nigel Farage to provide transparency about a £5 million gift he received from a billionaire businessman.  The UK borrowed more than expected in April due to high inflation, and the Office for National Statistics reported public sector net borrowing of £24.3 billion.

articles.title: US says DRC team must isolate due to Ebola before arriving for World Cup | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of Congo national football team must isolate for 21 days before entering the US for the World Cup due to an ongoing Ebola outbreak in their country.  Andrew Giuliani, executive director of the White House Task Force for the World Cup, confirmed this requirement, stating that the team must maintain a bubble until June 11th to avoid being denied entry. The team is currently training in Belgium and will play its first World Cup game against Portugal on June 17th in Houston.

articles.title: Waiting for Green Card? Leave US first, re-enter with an immigrant visa - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced new guidance directing immigration officers to require individuals on temporary visas, like B1/B2, F1/M1, J1, H-1B, and O-1, to return to their home countries while they wait for their Green Cards. This policy aims to distinguish between temporary admission and permanent residence, with the USCIS director, Joseph Edlow, stating that individuals seeking lawful permanent residency should apply for immigrant visas through the US Department of State before reentering the United States.

articles.title: Judith Chalmers, presenter of TV series Wish You Were Here, dies aged 90 | Television | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Judith Chalmers, the beloved British TV presenter who hosted Wish You Were Here…? for almost three decades, passed away at 90 after a battle with Alzheimer's disease. Her family said she died peacefully at home surrounded by loved ones.  She began her career in broadcasting at age 13 and went on to host numerous popular programs including Come Dancing and Woman’s Hour. Chalmers was known for her warm, approachable style and iconic sun tan, which became synonymous with the travel show. She is survived by her husband of 58 years, Neil Durden-Smith, and son Mark Durden-Smith, a TV presenter himself.

articles.title: US says temporary visa holders should leave to apply for Green Cards | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) issued new guidance stating that obtaining a Green Card within the US is discretionary, not automatic. The Department of Homeland Security said this policy aims to ensure immigration procedures are followed rather than allowing individuals to remain in the US while seeking permanent residency through "loopholes."  Rights groups criticized the move, warning it could force vulnerable migrants to return to unsafe conditions while awaiting decisions on their applications.

articles.title: ‘It would be a big mistake’: WHO Africa chief warns against underestimating Ebola virus risk in Congo, Uganda - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization's Africa director, Mohamed Yakub Janabi, warned against underestimating the risk of the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighboring Uganda.  He stated that a single case could trigger wider transmission, emphasizing the need for increased attention to the outbreak due to the lack of a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain. Janabi urged international cooperation to control the outbreak, highlighting the difficulty in assessing its duration due to the "hyperdynamic movement of people."  Efforts are underway to increase testing, strengthen infection prevention measures, and improve community engagement.

articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, Jaiñtia Students' Union
articles.rephrased_article: The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and those opposed to it engaged in violence, including the burning of a truck, leaving several people injured. The conflict followed similar clashes on Thursday near the District Magistrate’s office, where police used batons to disperse the groups.  The Jaiñtia National Council, Hima Sutnga Youth Federation, and Jaiñtia Students’ Union** stormed the public hearing site, leading to its cancellation.

articles.title: Wes Streeting insists he can win Labour leadership race despite ‘underdog’ status | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, former health secretary, launched a shadow campaign for the Labour leadership, arguing that Keir Starmer is unfit to lead.  He believes he can win over Labour members despite trailing in polls and being seen as right-leaning. Streeting outlined plans including moving families out of temporary accommodation, speeding up the establishment of a national care service, and introducing a wealth tax. He also suggested bringing back environmental impact assessments for large developments and addressing concerns about immigration.  Andy Burnham, who is campaigning to win a byelection in Makerfield, is seen as Streeting's main rival.

articles.title: Slovenia’s parliament approves right-wing Janez Jansa as prime minister | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Slovenia’s parliament voted to approve Janez Jansa, a right-wing populist, as prime minister.  Jansa's appointment follows a post-election stalemate and marks a shift from the country's previous liberal government. The new coalition government, formed by Jansa’s Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS) and several center-right groups, will hold 43 seats in the assembly. Jansa has previously served as prime minister from 2004 to 2008, 2012 to 2013, and 2020 to 2022.  He plans to prioritize economic growth, fighting corruption, and decentralization.

articles.title: Timelapse footage shows giant 'cave' inflated over Paris bridge
articles.rephrased_article: JR, a French artist known for his large-scale art installations, transformed Paris' oldest bridge, the Pont Neuf, overnight into a giant inflatable cave structure called "La Caverne" or "The Cave". The 17th-century landmark was nearly unrecognizable to Parisians until Thursday.  The installation, measuring 120 meters in length and ranging from 12-18 meters in height, will be open to the public starting June 6th and run until June 28th.

articles.title: Pakistan gets its own ‘Cockroach Awaam Party’ as India’s viral CJP sparks cross-border satire wave - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has seen the emergence of satirical political groups inspired by the Cockroach Janta Party, a viral movement in India.  These groups, such as the Cockroach Awami Party and Cockroach Awami League, have emerged on social media platforms like Instagram and X, mirroring the Indian party's focus on issues affecting unemployed youth, including education, healthcare, and employment opportunities. The Pakistani groups use similar slogans and branding to their Indian counterparts, positioning themselves as alternative voices to mainstream political parties in Pakistan.

articles.title: Public hearing for limestone mining called off in Meghalaya after protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: **The authorities in Meghalaya’s East Jaiñtia Hills district canceled a public hearing for a ₹1,800-crore integrated cement plant and limestone mining project after two groups clashed. Supporters of the project and opponents faced off at Lum Syrman, resulting in a truck being set ablaze and minor injuries to some people. The incident followed a similar clash near the District Magistrate’s office on Thursday, prompting police intervention.

articles.title: World Cup: England’s shock squad and the politics of football – The Latest | Soccer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Thomas Tuchel has selected a significantly different squad for England's World Cup team, omitting key players like Harry Maguire, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Cole Palmer, and Phil Foden. This decision comes as the club season concludes with Arsenal securing its first Premier League title in 22 years.

articles.title: Mahmoud Khalil to appeal US deportation case to Supreme Court | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Khalil, a pro-Palestine advocate, will appeal his deportation case to the Supreme Court after a federal appeals court declined to rehear his case.  Khalil's lawyers argue that he was targeted for his free speech and that the Trump administration exploited immigration enforcement to punish him. The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) supports Khalil's claim, stating that the government can't target individuals based on their protected speech.

articles.title: Power Division warns consumers against fake subsidy links, QR code scams - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Energy’s Power Division issued a warning to consumers about fraudulent activities targeting electricity bill subsidies. The Power Division advised against clicking on suspicious links or QR codes, as criminals are attempting to steal personal information through these methods.  Consumers were urged not to share any personal details for obtaining subsidies and law enforcement agencies have been informed of the scam.

articles.title: Why thousands of stock trades tied to Trump are raising eyebrows
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's name appears on government filings revealing thousands of stock trades made in the first three months of this year. The Trump Organization stated that neither the president, his family, nor the company were involved in selecting or approving investments and receive no advance notice of trading activity.

articles.title: Chudthebuilder Bond Offer: ChudTheBuilder may be released after reported $1M bond offer from crypto casino “Duel” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ChudTheBuilder, whose real name is Dalton Eatherly, may soon be released from jail after a crypto gambling platform called Duel offered to pay his $1 million bond. The news has generated significant online discussion, with many questioning the motivations behind the unusual financial offer in connection with the high-profile case involving serious charges related to a courthouse shooting in Tennessee.  The court has not yet confirmed final approval of the bond payment.

articles.title: Punjab government to remove stray dogs from high footfall public spaces following Supreme Court order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Chief Minister, announced that the state government will remove stray dogs from all high footfall public spaces as per Supreme Court directions issued on May 19, 2026.  The move aims to ensure public safety and provide relief to citizens concerned about stray dog attacks. The government plans to create adequate shelters for stray dogs while adhering to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and ABC Rules regarding euthanasia in cases involving dangerous or rabid animals.

articles.title: ‘Kind of humiliating’: trans community responds to EHRC’s new code of practice | Gender | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Whittle, a 70-year-old man who advocates for gender recognition, was at the Chelsea flower show when the updated code of practice from the Equality and Human Rights Commission was published. The guidance confirmed that single-sex spaces must be used based on biological sex, leading to mixed reactions. Some welcomed it as a consolidation of last year's court victory, while others expressed concern about its practical implications for trans inclusivity.  Businesses and service providers are grappling with the changes, seeking clarity and time to adapt their policies.

articles.title: Premier League finale: Arsenal, relegation, Champions League, Salah and Pep | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Premier League season concludes with all 10 matches kicking off simultaneously, featuring a relegation battle and European qualification fights. Arsenal will lift the title after Manchester City failed to win their match against Bournemouth.  Tottenham Hotspur and West Ham United are vying for survival in the final day's drama. Liverpool, Bournemouth, and Aston Villa are battling for Champions League spots, with Mohamed Salah's future at Liverpool uncertain after his public criticisms of the team's style.  Pep Guardiola is leaving Manchester City after a decade of success, with Enzo Maresca rumored to be his successor.

articles.title: ‘Most relentlessly cruel’: Gaza flotilla activists tell harrowing accounts of abuse in Israeli custody - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mousa Taher, a New Zealand activist, and other activists from the Global Sumud humanitarian aid flotilla, recounted harrowing experiences of abuse they endured while detained by Israeli forces.  Taher described being subjected to torture, including being bound tightly with plastic zip ties, having his face stepped on, and being beaten. He also said that Israeli soldiers recognized him and addressed him by name because he had previously been detained. Isselmou Ould Maloum, a Mauritanian activist, echoed similar accounts of violence, stating that the Israeli military lacks a strategy other than using force against Palestinians.  Gregory Terry, an American activist, described the detention as "miserable" and said his fellow activists suffered broken bones and were repeatedly tased. Juliet Lamont, an Australian activist, recounted being subjected to sexual assault and physical violence during their time on board the flotilla. All of these activists expressed their determination to continue protesting for Palestinian freedom.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma: Rival claims of murder and suicide set off media frenzy after Indian bride dies
articles.rephrased_article: A dowry death case in India has sparked a media frenzy after the death of 33-year-old model and actor Twisha Sharma.  Twisha's parents allege she was tortured by her husband, Samarth Singh, and his mother, retired judge Giribala Singh, over dowry demands and that she was murdered. The police have lodged a case against the Singhs and are investigating whether her death was murder or suicide. Giribala Singh denies the allegations, claiming Twisha had mental health issues and committed suicide.  The case has drawn attention to the issue of dowry deaths in India, where thousands of women are murdered annually for bringing insufficient dowries.

articles.title: UK pitched single market for goods with EU in pursuit of deeper trade ties | Brexit | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government proposed a single market for goods with the EU as a means to reintegrate British trade. However, EU officials rejected this idea and suggested alternatives like a customs union or economic alignment through the European Economic Area.  Despite these setbacks, both sides are seeking agreements on food and agricultural products, emissions trading schemes, and youth mobility programs. The UK government is also pursuing closer defense cooperation with the EU. While negotiations remain stalled on defining a future agenda, both sides hope to announce deals before a summit tentatively scheduled for July 13th.

articles.title: Lucky Motors partners with China's GAC as it bets fuel shock will drive EV switch - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Lucky Motors, a Pakistani conglomerate, is launching EVs in partnership with Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC) and plans local assembly by December 2026.  The move comes amid rising fuel prices and increased interest in solar energy, which the company believes will accelerate EV adoption. The CEO of Lucky Motors, Muhammad Faisal, expects initial imported stock to sell out quickly.  Lucky Motors, which also assembles smartphones, is exploring local battery manufacturing and plans to export Pakistani-assembled vehicles to other right-hand drive markets.

articles.title: What are the implications of US sanctions in Lebanon? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has imposed sanctions on nine individuals, including two Lebanese military officers, accused of ties to Hezbollah. The sanctions come as Israel continues its attacks on Lebanon despite a ceasefire and amid efforts by Washington to facilitate further talks between Lebanese and Israeli officials.

articles.title: French Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka cuts short news conference as top players protest over Grand Slam prize money - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Aryna Sabalenka, Iga Swiatek, and other top players protested the French Open's prize money by limiting their media commitments to 15 minutes.  The players, who are demanding a higher percentage of revenue be allocated to prize money, player welfare, and more consultation in decision-making, believe the current system is inadequate. Novak Djokovic did not participate but supported the principle behind the action. The French Open tournament director expressed confidence that the issue will be resolved while players remain open to further discussions.

articles.title: 'West wants to impose homosexuality on the rest of the world': Senegal PM makes shocking claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Senegal's Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko defended the country's new anti-LGBTQ law, arguing that it reflects the will of the Senegalese people and is not influenced by Western pressure.  Sonko criticized Western countries, accusing them of imposing their values on other nations. He stated that while Senegal faces criticism from some international organizations like the UN, they do not have to follow these practices. The new law significantly increases penalties for same-sex relations in the country, prompting concern from human rights groups and activists.

articles.title: Mumbai, Maharashtra emerging as key hubs for global investment and clean energy partnerships, say diplomats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Consul Generals from Australia and Finland highlighted the growing investment opportunities in Mumbai and Maharashtra, emphasizing infrastructure development, clean energy, education, and technology sectors.  They praised Mumbai's transformation, citing projects like the Coastal Road and metro expansion as drivers of investor confidence. Both diplomats acknowledged challenges faced by foreign investors, including regulatory clarity and streamlined approval systems. Despite these challenges, they expressed optimism about Mumbai's long-term trajectory as a global economic hub.

articles.title: Meta and Snapchat blocking Saudi dissidents’ accounts | Social media | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Meta, Instagram, and X have blocked accounts of Saudi Arabian dissidents, following orders from the Saudi government. The move has been met with criticism from human rights groups who argue that these companies are effectively silencing dissent and aiding in repression.  At least seven accounts were blocked by Meta at the end of April, including those of two American citizens and two individuals based in Europe. Snapchat appears to have slowed or removed some accounts without notifying users, while X, owned by Elon Musk, has informed some users that their content was blocked due to a request from the Saudi government.

articles.title: US releases second batch of government declassified UFO files - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States’ Defense Department released a second batch of classified files on alleged UFO sightings, including reports of green orbs, discs, and fireballs.  These documents, ordered by President Donald Trump, follow a disclosure process that began in the late 1970s. The release includes documentation from a top-secret facility in Sandia, New Mexico, where there were 209 reported sightings between 1948 and 1950. Experts have said the first batch of released files did not provide conclusive evidence of alien technology or extraterrestrial life.

articles.title: San Diego’s Muslims, a mosque, and a city shaken | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Diego Muslim community is grieving after an attack that shattered their sense of safety.  The attack has prompted the community to come together and support each other as they try to move forward.

articles.title: Carney says Alberta is 'essential' to Canada as province plans vote on separation
